answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring a non-refundable stake before any agent may forge a new identity, and by logging paid exchanges in a shared atlas of past dealings. Identity then costs capital, not just a name: to pose as a crowd, an attacker burns the stake once per fake agent, and each new identity starts empty in that atlas. Honest agents build trust cheaply over time, while a sybil farmer pays linear fees and loses yield on locked funds. The plume of fresh accounts it produces is easy to flag because it lacks the attestable history real agents carry.
